evidence:
Reachability: every capability graded is obtainable in the provided runtime. The agent image (environment/Dockerfile) has Node 22, express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 under NODE_PATH, copies /assets and /instructions, and runs as root with network_mode="public" (task.toml:22), so in-browser self-testing tools can be fetched if wanted. integration.md:3 states exactly the launch contract test.sh:97-111 uses (node /app/server.js as uid 65534, env -i with PATH/NODE_PATH/HOME/PORT=3000/DB_PATH; test.sh:87 chowns /app so a fresh app.db can be created). Seed data supplies every fixture the criteria use (K-1 11 days old on 7-day M-11, K-10 exactly 7 days and K-11 one second younger, K-13 with earlier version '2,400', held K-2 with earlier 'Landlords notice recieved.', K-16 with literal tags, Dev walled from M-12, clock 2026-05-12T11:00:00Z). Accounts/password are public (walls-and-retention.md:3-11). Achievability is measured: the raw-evidence-index entries for golden-run.log hash-match and their matching_source_files hash-match the frozen solution/server.js, app.js, seed and solve.sh; golden-run.log shows all 16 functional criteria, gate_constraints, persistence_before/after and all 6 polish rows PASS on these bytes (scripted Playwright, not a configured judge run; render/visual not scripted).

Ambiguity sweep (each graded demand traced to one reading): walls give only a plain 'not available' for any direct reach (walls-and-retention.md:17), covering the cross-matter reply and client M-12 post refusals; exact-seven-day deletion and edit-does-not-rejuvenate (walls:23); hold covers only that message and release applies the timer at once (walls:29); search is case-insensitive literal character matching with %,_,* not wildcards (walls:33), which naturally means substring ('urvey booked'); transcript is a page with an address, oldest first in threads, versions only for held edited messages (walls:35); mark-unread 'moves the line there' (conversations.md:25) fixes the count-1 reading in unread leg 3; stale-edit refusal keeps typed text (conversations:9); same-time order consistency is explicitly tied to the fixed clock (integration.md:7). Where the brief leaves an implementation choice, the criteria accept alternatives (wall_every_route JUDGE-W3 either refused or filed in its own parent's matter; versions viewer and suggestion request are conditional in timer_changes / wall_mentions_and_links; any endpoint shape, any time format, page-or-dialog confirm). The previous-bytes model run's four functional failures (mention regex bug, timestamp-based unread marker, transcript omitting held versions, which the brief states explicitly) were implementation defects against unambiguous text, not alternative readings.

Notes (not defects, no grading impact found): (1) No sign-out control is named in the brief, though signin_and_client_scope and polish refusal_in_place say 'Sign out'; this is implied by 'sign in as different people' (instruction.md:9) and the skill lists house-convention identity surfaces as a known false positive. (2) Seed read_up_to semantics (chronological vs threaded display order) are undocumented, e.g. Gwen M-11 read to K-3 gives 4 unread chronologically vs 2 in display order, but no criterion grades a seeded unread number (unread leg 4 says 'at least 2'; persistence compares before/after; visual matter_sidebar does not grade counts). (3) Internal workbook annotation still says 'no network'; the public sheet and the skill profile say public network, which this task follows. Tried counterexamples: an FTS word-token search would fail 'urvey booked' but contradicts 'exactly the characters typed'; an idempotency check placed before the access check could answer Gwen's M-12 replay with a 200 duplicate, but the brief's wall/client 'nothing but not available' rule makes access-first the only conforming order (golden server.js:395-415 checks visibility before client_key). No unreachable item or second reasonable reading that a criterion would penalise was found.
